resolved_levels_check: PASS - Omastar 48+1-2=47, Runerigus 48+1-2=47, Mega Slowbro 48+0-2=46, Relicanth 48+2-2=48, all matching the driver at level_cap 48. No --cap adjustment.

attempts.note: Rillaboom + Magnezone + Alakazam + Weavile + Gengar + Spiritomb. Lost Magnezone on turn 1 to a critical Earth Power - a 4x hit into an Electric/Steel body that was my own build error rather than a difficulty signal. After that the room folded fast: Wood Hammer 4x one-shot Omastar, priority Grassy Glide 4x one-shot Choice Band Relicanth before it could use its second Head Smash, and one Dark Pulse removed Mega Slowbro. Runerigus was the only member that put up a fight, stalling two turns behind Protect.

strategy_checks.check: Omastar takes a safe Shell Smash when the board allows, and White Herb erases the drops
strategy_checks.evidence: Omastar never used Shell Smash. On turn 1 it chose Earth Power into Magnezone, which was the correct read and got a critical KO, and it died to Wood Hammer on that same turn. The dossier's own note that 'nothing protects Omastar's Shell Smash turn' is confirmed in play: against any Grass lead it simply does not survive to set up.

strategy_checks.check: Runerigus burns or attacks the relevant threat rather than guarding emptily
strategy_checks.evidence: turn 2 Will-O-Wisp burned Rillaboom, my only physical attacker and the member killing its whole team - an excellent read. Turn 3 Poltergeist into Spiritomb was real damage. The turn-1 and turn-4 Protects are the exception, see protect ledger and AI defect.

strategy_checks.check: Wandering Spirit's contact-triggered ability exchange actually threatens the player's abilities
strategy_checks.evidence: the threat was real enough to shape my whole plan - Rillaboom never attacked Runerigus because losing Grassy Surge to a swap would have cost the terrain, and I routed its U-turn into Mega Slowbro instead. No exchange fired because I respected it.

strategy_checks.check: Mega Slowbro has a separate Calm Mind endgame
strategy_checks.evidence: Slowbro Mega Evolved on entry and chose Ice Beam, then died to a single 2x Dark Pulse before a second turn. Its 186 HP at level 46 is not enough to reach the Calm Mind plan against cap-48 special Dark damage.

strategy_checks.check: Choice Band Relicanth applies immediate physical pressure
strategy_checks.evidence: turn 2 Head Smash into Rillaboom, which is exactly the authored alternate deployment; it just lost the speed race to priority Grassy Glide.

protect_ledger.payoff: EMPTY - both of my attacks that turn were aimed at Omastar and nothing was ever directed at Runerigus. Mitigating: under the no-command-reads rule the AI was forecasting against two attackers with a 2x Grass option, so a guard was not unreasonable, but the realised payoff was zero.
REAL - blocked Gengar's Psychic and Spiritomb's Dark Pulse, the latter a 2x hit on a 77 HP body, and bought a full turn plus a Leftovers and grassy-terrain heal.

ai_defect_note: No illegal or nonsensical choice. The turn-1 Runerigus Protect produced no payoff but is defensible as an expected-value guard on an opening board; it is logged in the Protect ledger rather than raised as a defect because the same battler's turn-4 Protect was correctly timed and it never guarded twice in a row.
calibration_reasoning: First-attempt win with a single player faint, and that faint was a critical hit into a type error of my own rather than pressure Foster applied. That triggers the brief's '+1 on the opponent's weakest one or two members, never the ace/Mega/legend first' rule. Mega Slowbro sits at offset 0 but is excluded as the Mega, so the two +1 members are Omastar and Runerigus, both moving 1 -> 2. Relicanth is left at +2 because a Choice Band Rock Head body is already the room's hardest hitter.
rerun_status: NOT RERUN. The level change cannot take effect in this benchmark: the headless driver reads trainer parties out of the prebuilt ROM in work/agent-battle-build-2, and rebuilding is explicitly the main agent's step (this agent is instructed never to run make). The teams-file edit is left in the working tree uncommitted for the wave-boundary rebuild and rerun.
could_this_be_cooler: Keep the fossil-diver concept - White Herb Shell Smash, Rock Head Head Smash and a Wandering Spirit body are three genuinely distinct ideas for one route ace. But this run confirms the dossier's own flagged weakness sharply rather than softly: Omastar is the designated setup piece and it died on turn 1 without ever setting up, because every single member of this team is 2x or 4x weak to Grass and nothing on the team can deny a Grass lead a turn. The concrete improvement I would recommend is the one already flagged - give the room one Fake Out or redirection body so Omastar's Shell Smash turn is bought rather than hoped for. Relicanth is the natural candidate to lose a slot for it, since Choice Band Head Smash and post-Smash Omastar are doing the same job. Recommended, not applied in this pass.
legality_problems_found: None. All four authored sets resolved cleanly.
notes: Player-side note: Magnezone is 4x weak to Ground and Omastar carries Earth Power, so it is a poor lead into this room despite being the obvious Electric answer to three Water-types.
scope: Synthetic headless benchmark through scripts/playthrough/battle_driver.py against work/agent-battle-build-2. Not earned campaign traversal.
